TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded) I own the TOZO T10, and I can't say enough great things about them, but alas, I stupidly left one where the puppy could get it, and now I have one ear that still performs, but the 'button' no longer works (amazing that it didn't break).

I probably should have bought another pair of the T10s, but the T6s had pretty amazing specs, so I took a chance.

First, the pros; AMAZING sound, noise isolation, fit, and sensitive fingerprint controls (no pressing). I have over ear Bose, and Beats, and these could stand against their sound quality any day.

Now the cons: you can't roam far from the phone, computer or iPad you're connected to, or the bluetooth will drop you. In fact, if a butterfly farts in the amazon, these earbuds will drop their connection to your bluetooth device. The other stand-out con is battery life. I don't know if mine were defective, but they NEVER had the battery that I enjoyed with the T10s, and they seem to be getting worse. The case will hold a charge when stored for well over a week, but the buds last about four hours with music playing in them. If you're just wearing them at the gym for an hour or two, they're fine, but if you're wearing them to drown out office noise, you're going to be out of luck after lunch.

I am considering handing these off to one of the younger people in my family who need a spare pair to use while their primary pair is charging. If TOZO comes out with a new model, I may wait to see if the folks reviewing it have the same issues. I'm actively looking for the old T10s in the meantime.
text_fidelity_b: TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded)

text_fidelity_a:
SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V I really wanted to like this product, but it just didn't work out.

First of all, you need to have a really good, smooth, white surface (preferably a dedicated movie screen) to achieve the optimum results. A very, very dark room would also help. Yes, of course you could use the wall, a bed sheet or some other improvised backdrop, but it would defeat the whole point of seeing a film in the manner this projector was designed for.

Also, you must put up a credit card in order to use any of the channels available to you. Even if you are only accessing the free channels. And between you and me, I'm not that excited watching the NASA channel nonstop. You could use your Prime membership to watch movies, but that wasn't so great either.

Other reviewers have suggested it would be terrific for a slumber party. Really? What's the matter with your big screen T.V.? The picture quality is excellent but the sound is not up to par. If you're gonna go this far then you really need to be firing on all cylinders with the sound and the picture.

In conclusion, this is really a disappointment. I had hoped I could watch baseball or something else of interest to me, but this projector requires too many variables to line up perfectly, and it's just not worth the time or the effort.

The one positive - it's really cute and small.
text_fidelity_b: SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V

text_fidelity_a: Mini Projector, Meer YG220 Pico LCD Video Projector for Children Present,Home Theater,Game,Outdoor Entertainment with HDMI USB AV Micro SD Input and Remote Control [[VIDEOID:31c0baac202ec9459a67e0db40c729c]] First, I have to say that this projector reminds me of the character 'Eva' from the movie Wall-e'. Next, It's simple enough for kids to set up and use. It doesn't require any special changes in your laptops settings, it will automatically select the HDMI port for display (at least mine did). The LED projection looks just a little pixelated if you're real close to it. But, from a regular viewing distance it looks just fine. The built in speaker has good quality sound. The clip that I included with my review is from one of my own videos. The projection was on an off white wall, about 8 feet away. That should give you some kind of idea of what the projection will look like for you. Also the room was not very dark. This might be the happiest I've been with some earphones since my beloved Nuforce NE-700X. But to be fair those cost $90 in 2014.

Update after 2 weeks of use:

I went to a larger tip and now they don't sit as far in my ear. The bass and soundstage both improved with more air around the instruments. I really like these. I don't find myself thinking oh they do this, or they don't do that with regard to sound. The just play the music. That little TINY bit of graininess is gone with some break in I guess. While I don't listen to Metal or EDM they handle all genres of music well and handle more complex music like rock well compared to others I have tried. They come with 4 size tips so finding the right size is easier compared to pairs that only come with 3 size tips. The tips grip the nozzle really well but still come off and go on pretty easily. They do not go really loud but they do go loud enough for me.I haven't played with EQ much because I haven't felt the need. Wires are thin and tangle pretty easily and don't untangle very easily. I have not noticed any microphonics. Of course, I'd like to have $100 buds but for $55 dollars they hit my nice but I won't cry if I lose them price point.

===========================================
Original review

They are not even broken in yet (and they don't need it) but my only real complaint and it's nitpicky, but they have a touch of graininess. But nowhere near as much as the Carbo Tenor. These are very neutra with decent detail while never being too bright. There is nice seperation between instruments but not much of a soundstage but there is nice amount of 'air' around the intruments. They do not have a lot of extension but they are not bass shy like the Carbo Tenor were. Drums sound natural, again not like the Carbo Tenor where they sounded more like carboard boxes.

They are very light so they very comfortable. (I like straight earphones the best) The default tips fit me the best which is a nice change for me. There is next to no strain relief on the earphones as you can see in the picture so if you are hard on headphones, maybe consider other phones. on the good side the lack of strain relief makes them very comfortable worn wire up which i want for the gym. They have vents on the back so I doubt that isolation is very good for in-ear phones.

In summary these are nuetral sounding with out any of the 'problems' of hifi. They are never over sibilant and they do not punish badly recorded songs or when listening to low bit rate stuff like pandora. I would call them fun for working out but they are not too dry if the quality of the music is what you want. They are not going to impress anyone or give you an eargasm when listening to your best music. But at $54 I'm extemely please with them and for me are a big step up from the Carbo Tenor unless you are impressed by a forward/blaring sound.

text_fidelity_a: Roku 3 Streaming Media Player (2014 model) Without repeating what everyone has said here, I will speak for Roku's support of the Plex media streaming software which is a free Roku channel. If you have never heard of it, it is a fantastic solution that allows you to use Roku (as well as all your portable devices and remote computers, including ones on the internet-at-large) to stream all of the movies on your computer, regardless of the format. On Roku, you can browse the movie collection on your computer using a slick interface and watch it in full resolution. (This is only if you have a fast connection like a home wireless network, and you need to configure it to do this- an easy settings change.) If your computer can play it, so can your Roku. The key to this is because all the transcoding of the video file happens on your computer so all Roku has to do is play the video stream. The result is that you can easily fast-forward and rewind, as well and have the jump-back feature like the TiVo has. This was the primary reason that I bought the Roku as it is a lot easier to use than trying to connect your computer directly to your TV and muddling about with computer controls to watch movies. The Plex interface on Roku is easy to use and very slick. It does nice things like look up movie data so you have the cover art, theme music, and movie info for you to peruse as you are browsing your library. Finally, there is the "Plex it!" feature which you can use with your computer's browser, so that when you find a video on the internet on your computer, you want to queue it up for later to watch on your TV, and it will appear in your movie queue in Plex on Roku, regardless of the video format! This also gets around the one annoying thing about Roku and that it doesn't have a native YouTube channel for some reason.
text_fidelity_b: Roku 3 Streaming Media Player (2014 model)

CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition This is a very complete kit and does contain everything you need to setup a Raspberry Pi 3. Yes, the op system installs easily and, with luck, you can be up and running in less than an hour. So, why the 2 stars?

It gets 2 stars because the Raspberry Pi is probably one of the most frustrating devices I've ever tried to put to any real use. For example, I wanted to set it up so I could use a VNC server on the Pi and a VNC client on my Mac (OS X El Capitan). After three days of almost non-stop failures, I'm sick of this thing. Researching how to get this task done leads you down a black hole of internet articles and posts on the Raspberry Pi site, most of that give different instructions, use different commands, tell you which files to edit and what to put in them, and almost none work, period!

The core problem rests squarely on the Raspberry Pi organization. Their own website is full of conflicting posts on how to do just about anything beyond a basic setup. Few, if any posts state which model of Pi is being referenced, and many bear no date. All in all, it's a very frustrating experience and, while I like to tinker with these things, a little success is required once in a while to keep me chugging along. I think I'm done with this thing. I had hoped it would finally be a Linux for the rest of us. Unfortunately, it's just as convoluted and difficult to use as any version of Linux out there (my opinion).

However, if you're looking to explore the Pi, this kit has everything you need to do a basic setup of Linux. And, should you want to use it as a web server, file server, media server, you're really on your own. Drink lots of coffee and plan to pull our lots of hair.
text_fidelity_b: CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition

Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras Although this lens is intended for macro photography, it's also a great lens for general purpose shots, or portrait shots. The lens produces beautiful sharp images and is a fast, accurate focuser. The lens is moderately heavy and bulky, so I wouldn't classify it as eminently carryable, and without image stabilization, you might suffer hand shake blur if you're not shooting at the wide end; at smaller apertures, using it with a tripod is highly recommended. But if you're buying it primarily to get into macro this shouldn't much matter as tripod shooting with macro is virtually a necessity, and completely expected.

The 100mm focal length is a nice compromise when you want to get close to small subjects (particularly insects) but are limited to how close you can get before scaring the subject off - as a comparison with the 180mm macro, you would want to factor in a consideration as to what you might like to shoot most of the time - big spiders that you'd rather stay well away from might be an application more suited to the 180mm, for instance, but if you are keen to shoot mostly flowers, the 180 might be more length than you really need.

In short, the 100mm macro is one of my "keeper" lenses, a real performer.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

I figured I’d compare the newest of both to make my final decision and although the Oasis has some light features I like, I chose this Paperwhite because the side bar (where you hold it and flip pages?) on the Oasis is just ugly to me. I don’t like that it’s only on one side making the whole thing off center. I primarily wanted a Kindle so I could get off of my phone more often to just read and I also needed something that provided a more natural experience for my eyes. My favorite feature of the Kindle is that I can put it on dark mode with the black background and white text. I even keep my iPhone at the lowest light setting with dark mode too to spare my eyes the brightness 24/7.

This Kindle is exactly what I’ve been looking for. It’s lightweight, slim, very easy to hold, and turning pages is a breeze. No clicking buttons, just a tap on the screen. I paired it with the leather amazon case in plum to match and it’s perfect. Sleek and beautiful. The light options are perfect for day and night reading, I can even see it perfectly with zero eye strain in a pitch black room. The screen looks remarkably like a real print book and it’s just so simple to use. I was initially concerned about the ads being too intrusive, but it turns out that they’re only on the lock screen and they just advertise books to read. I don’t mind them at all. My Kindle is only a week old so I can’t speak to much else yet, but I’ve been using it daily all week and the battery is at 97% right now without any recharge so that gives me hope for it lasting going forward. I’m very happy with so far and have found that because it doesn’t do anything like a tablet or phone would do, I’m reading more without such distractions. Leaving my phone down more too. Love it.

Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter I have one of the 77mm versions of this variable neutral density for cutting sunlight to manageable levels when shooting video outdoors. It works fine. I assume this 58mm version will work with typical Tiffen quality as well.

For those of you who might want to use it in conjunction with your factory lens hood, forget it.

The attaching thread is 58mm in diameter, but the outer diameter is 70.1 mm -- way bigger than the sunshade.

The front ring is threaded, but apparently only so the retaining ring can hold the front polarizer in place. The front thread measures out to 66.34mm to the inside of the thread (top of thread), or about 66.5 mm to the bottom of the thread groove. 67mm lens hoods exist and may fit, but not sure.

For my 77mm filter, I found a spare rubber lens shade that happened to be the same outer diameter as the filter and attached it with some electrician's tape. Works fine for longer lenses like the 70-200mm but vignettes on the 24mm end of the 24-70mm.

May need a matte box.

Comes in a very well built ballistic nylon pouch with Velcro closure and a very handy vinyl business card-sized window so you can label the thing and know what's inside.

It's a great filter that lets you shoot at 1/50 of a second at ISO 200 with the lens opened up to wider apertures to achieve shallow depth of field in bright sunlight. I find myself adjusting exposure by turning the filter a bit instead of changing f/stop.

Highly recommended. Just remember that you may be fighting flare unless you can rig up a sunshade, French flag or a matte box to keep the sun off it.

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 6 camera kit - Eco Packaging (VMS3630B) This is a truly wireless security camera system. The cameras operate on four CR123 batteries each, and lithium-ion batteries are included. That's a big plus, because you can install the cameras most anywhere. Setup took me a little over an hour.

It might be costly to replace lithium-ion batteries regularly, so you might consider getting rechargeable batteries.

The cameras are not pan-tilt-zoom cams. They're fixed. But the mounts are little metal domes, so you can manually aim the camera most any way you choose. The cameras have strong magnets in them to stick them firmly to the mounts. You can also stick the cameras to any steel or iron surface. You might keep in mind that since they're only held by magnets, the cams could be stolen easily if located in easy reach.

You start setup by downloading and installing the Arlo app on your device (phone, tablet, etc.) Then you create an account, agree to the terms, and follow the on-screen instructions for setup. The free version of the app supports up to six cameras.

The Netgear Arlo camera receiver/router connects to your Internet router with an Ethernet cable. It has a wall power supply with a six-foot cord. After it establishes a connection with the Internet router, you then pair the cameras, one by one, with the camera router. That takes about twenty seconds each.

This is where annoying things started. The app has motion detection on by default. Six cameras started slamming my email inbox and notification banner with motion detection alerts. It took a while to find the switch to turn motion detection off. You get to it by clicking on "mode" at the top, then the name you gave your camera system, then click on "disarm."

There's no batch delete feature in the app (not one I could find anyway) to delete all those motion detection videos at once. I had to go through and delete them one by one.

Notifications said the base unit and all the cams needed firmware updates. The update for the base unit went smoothly. The camera updates did not go so smoothly. Almost all of them said "update failed - camera rejected upgrade request." I moved the cameras close to the base unit and retried the updates, one camera at a time. Success.

These cameras do not continually take pictures, which is probably a battery saving feature. They start taking video or pictures only when motion detection is triggered, or when you manually click on "live" on each camera's thumbnail picture. The live stream takes several seconds to start. So the best setting for security would be motion detection active, but that might mean a lot of notifications. If you want to just take a look at the cameras to see what's up currently, that's kind of a problem. Each camera has to be started, and there's several seconds of wait time. (Edited to add: Adding to the wait time is that it appears video clips are not stored locally but rather uploaded to the manufacturer's site then downloaded back to your device.)

Let me put it this way: If motion detection is switched off and you hear the sound of a varmint on your porch and you want to take a quick look or grab a quick snapshot with one of these cameras, that's just not going to happen. You have to rely on motion detection being on to take the pictures for you. With motion detection off, at best you'll be able to take a look after several seconds of camera startup and buffering. (Edited to add: And if the varmint is moving quickly, you may not get a picture of it at all---just the motion detection alert and a short video that didn't capture what set the alert off.)

In contrast, I have three IP cameras that are always on. I can open the app for them and see a live picture from all three cams at once and grab a snapshot from any of them. But they all require hard-wired power, so it's a trade-off.

When you start the app, you see thumbnails from the last time you ran the live streams, or from the last motion detection. Those thumbnails can be hours old. I don't know if it would be possible, but if the Arlo app and cams had a "refresh all thumbnails" feature, that would be a big help in getting a current look at all your cameras. Then you could start live streams if you choose to.

For some reason the app will only support running five live streams out of the six cameras. You have to stop one of the streams to start the sixth.

If you install the Arlo app on more than one device, only one can be logged in and viewing cams at a time.

(Edited to add: A couple of other issues with the app: If you haven't opened the app in a while, you may get a notice that your login token has expired and you have to re-enter your password. More seconds lost if you got a motion detect alert and want to take a quick look. And sometimes you have to dismiss an ad before you can go look at the cams. And on my Kindle Fire, the Arlo app tends to go into some sort of loop sometimes, and I have to shut down and reboot the device.)

Picture quality is good. It can be set to lower resolution to maximize battery life, or medium or high resolution. The cams also have a night vision mode that can be switched off individually using the app. This is handy if you want to position the camera to look out a window at night. If the night vision mode is on, the IR led will reflect off the window at night like a bright light. Turning off night vision mode will avoid that. However, this still requires the exterior to be well lit or to have an outdoor IR source. The cameras' built in IR illumination isn't long range. It will light an average size room though.

The manufacturer says the cameras are weatherproof and can be positioned outdoors.

The web site says the cameras have a 300-foot range line-of-sight. One camera I placed about fifty feet from the router had difficulty connecting. It seems that the number of walls and other items between the camera and the router can have a big effect on connection, which isn't unusual with any wireless devices.

I think for a basic security system, IP cameras might have a few advantages over this system. But this system has its points, such as install-anywhere convenience and fairly simple setup. For actual security, keeping the system motion-detection armed and just letting the cameras grab and upload pictures and the app send notifications is the best solution, I would think. If you want to monitor live pictures yourself, or even just glance at very current pictures from time to time, I'd think this system wouldn't be a workable solution.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 6 camera kit - Eco Packaging (VMS3630B)

This is NOT the speaker that you simply grab and throw in the bag and go. This speaker is rather large and surprisingly VERY heavy.

The sound quality is nice but the bass is only ok in my opinion. I have another speaker which is made by Amazon that cost about $50 that has the exact same sound quality. It is loud but as with this bass, ive heard others that are louder and cost much less.

I will start with the app that the instructions tell you that you need to download. It states that it is for updates, but all I saw is that it is used for is linking multiple speakers together.

I wanted this speaker because we spend alot of time out by the pool and at the river during the summer. I knew that I wanted something that was water proof for both of those settings so I was happy to give this one a try. As I mentioned before, this sucker is HEAVY so while it may be water proof, if you were to drop in the river at any point it would go straight to the bottom never to be seen again, so it wouldn't really matter how water proof it is. For the pool and sitting stationary, it would be perfect.

One use that I can see us using this speaker would be for travel baseball games. It is loud enough that you would be able to hear it from a distance.

As I said earlier... some will love this speaker and think that it is absolutely worth it. Others will not. This speaker will strictly come down to personal opinion. For instance, other than the weight, I love this speaker. My spouse thinks that his $50 is much better.

The xb33 with just two woofers has almost no mids and the highs are muddy at best. The xb33 DOES play much LOUDER then the x55, so for parties this would be the better choice. text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I first became enamored of the garmin company after using the one with a rental car. The ease of use and accuracy was impressive. Unfortunately, that model is no longer in production so I opted for this unit.

In general I am pleased. Easy to set up, the unit features a bright, clear screen. It is a snap to use and the directions have been unfailing accurate. I drive alot and so far have used this unit throughout New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, DC and Virginia. I have had no problem with reception even while traversing mountainous regions. I appreciate the advance notice for turns and the voice command system is a convenience.

However, this unit is not flawless. The robotic voice often mispronounces street names and the voice command system seems a bit hard of hearing when it comes to addresses. I have had to pull over and type in the address. The unit does not like to deviate from its chosen route. For instance, one location I frequent in New York is accessible both by the thruway (toll road) and other non-toll main arteries. Both are about the same distance. When I want to avoid the toll route, the unit will recalculate directing that I turn around and follow the initial route multiple times before adjusting to the alternate route. A big deal, no,but annoying nonetheless. While I have not been terribly plagued by the pop ups, they are annoying and potentially unsafe. While the start up guide and manual are adequate, they are barely so. Whatever happened to detailed instructions? But my biggest gripe is the customer service. I called twice with questions and had ridicualously long waits of fifteen minutes and twenty-five minutes respectively. There is no round the clock service. The last time I called it wasnt even available all week, totally unacceptable.

So while I like this system,there is room for improvement.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Logitech ConferenceCam Connect All-in-One Video Collaboration Solution for Small Groups – Full HD 1080p Video, USB and Bluetooth Speakerphone, Plug-and-Play The Conference Cam Connect is a great device for video conferencing, it is compact, portable, and easy to set up. This video conferencing system connects easily up by either USB or Bluetooth and is ready to use right away. While being small and portable, it is full of features.
The camera delivers good quality video capability, the video is crisp and clear and bright, it does not have any framing or freezing issues that occur in other systems I have used. The remote is a very handy addition to to the device and is the best way to control the unit, it allows panning, zooming, muting, and volume control.

The device is battery powered, compact, and portable, and connects wirelessly via Bluetooth. This allows you to move the device around to different areas without losing connectivity if so desired. This lens has excellent image quality. It is rugged and features Pentax professional quality glass. It was build for Pentax by Tamron. That means you can save about $600 when you opt for this lens instead of paying the premium price of the 70-200 f/2.8 Pentax lens. I'd recommend mounting this lens with a tripod adapter made for the Tamron 70-210 f/4.0 (it is a perfect fit because that lens is the same barrel, but, it doesn't have the Pentax lens elements). This lens is one of my favorites, no doubt.

USB Type C Cable, USB-A to USB-C Red Durable Braided Fast Charging Cable, Compatible with iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, Samsung Galaxy S21/S10/S9/Plus, Google Pixel 5/C/3/2/XL, DLC5203RA/37 Thank you in advance to the Amazon VINE program for providing an item to review. A positive review was not required, nor was it requested, and all words are my own.

One thing I sadly use a lot of – phone/USB cables for charging and data transfer. These are almost as bad as the AUX cables for my car and iPod.

So, seeing this was a Philips one – I honestly thought I lucked out. I was going to give my old cable to my mom as hers was cracking near the "C" port. I figured I could use this one - she could have my old one.

It is a DURABLE cable and looked like it would go through quite a bit. The length is perfect for charging with an adapter connected to a power strip on the floor. And, it can also plug into the USB ports on a computer (or so equipped power strip).

So, why a one star rating?

This does not work. I tried with my phone and my mom’s phone. NADA. Nothing. I tried connecting it to the adapter – nothing. Tried using just the USB cable to a USB port on a power strip (which was on since it is powering my computer) – NOTHING.

So, I tried using a USB port on my computer. NOTHING. Tried with a “USB hub” connected to my computer. There was a slight problem. The “buttons” on the port light up when a port is turned on. Despite the port for this cord being on – the lights didn’t light up. Other items connected – my external mouse and a USB flash drive – they were turned off when this cord was connected.

Needless to say – this is BELOW one star. It doesn’t even work. But, I do have to rate it something.

I could’ve gotten a bad cable – after all, there is no damage to it or the packaging. But, it still doesn't work. But, I can’t return it since it was free.

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight Ultra-Bright LED 36 Camera / Video Light with Rechargeable Battery Pack and Charger for Canon, Nikon, Olympus, Pentax DSLR, Mini-DSLR and Camcorders This is an great value in a light panel. While the size limits the amount of light output (compared with larger models made by Bestlight) the size makes this far more workable on smaller cameras.

I've used a couple of their larger models, and they are fine for hefty DSLRs. But, when put on a smaller camera it makes it so top-heavy that it topples over. This one, however, is so small and light (it is less than 2.5 inches wide and weights only 2.1 ounces including the battery) that it worked fine on my Powershot without making it top-heavy.

Now, the size does limit the light output – this is nowhere near as powerful as their larger models. It also does not have variable light output as the larger models do. It just has an on/off switch. But for general lighting tasks, it works very well.

It comes with an internal lithium battery that is rated at 1200mAh and a charger for the battery. The battery is small and adds little weight to the device. I find that to be a big plus, since many of their larger models don’t come with a battery. On the downside, this will not run on AA batteries like their larger models do, so when the battery is dead you’ll have some downtime until it recharges (unless you buy a spare battery).

It has a hot shoe attachment for mounting on the camera. It can also be mounted on a tripod or light stand. The mount is plastic but reasonably well made. Note: although it has a hot shoe, it does not communicate with the camera in any way. You have to manually turn it on/off.

It does not come with filters, so the color temperature is limited to 6500K. That's a good point for general use, however.

This is a great choice for smaller cameras or for when you want to add some light but don’t want to deal with a larger unit. It’s easy to toss into a camera bag and carry along. The performance is excellent and the build quality is quite good given the price (especially since a battery and charger is included). Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight Ultra-Bright LED 36 Camera / Video Light with Rechargeable Battery Pack and Charger for Canon, Nikon, Olympus, Pentax DSLR, Mini-DSLR and Camcorders

No problem with the connection to the network. I purchased an Anker because I consider them to be just as good, if not better than OEM equipment.

Once I arrived at home, I hooked up my phone to charge it. I instantly got the dreaded Samsung water drop. The USB-C was as dry as a bone when I plugged it in. I tried every recommended method of remedying the problem, to no avail.

I issued a return request to Amazon and they instantly issued me a full refund. The problem is that I have to use a Qi charger now because the USB-C port is damaged. To be fair, this is the second Samsung product I have owned where the charging port was damaged even though I have not used your typical gas station charging cable on either my S8 or my S20.

While I hold Anker harmless, and Amazon did the right thing by me, I still must issue a caveat emptor warning. If I am upset with anyone, it's Samsung.
